text:
Using screw gauge of pitch 0.1 cm and
50 divisions on its circular scale, the thickness
of an object is measured. It should correctly be
recorded as
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using a screw gauge of pitch 0.1 cm and 50 divisions on its circular scale, the thickness of an object is measured as:

Measurement = (Main scale reading) + (Circular scale reading × Least count)

where the least count is calculated as the pitch of the screw gauge divided by the number of divisions on the circular scale:

Least count = (Pitch of screw gauge) / (Number of circular scale divisions)

Least count = $\frac{0.1}{50}$ = 0.002 cm

Now if we multiply division of circular scale with least count then we get $0^{th}$ digit of fraction part even. 

Here only option B has $0^{th}$ digit of fraction part even.

text:
Model a torch battery of length $l$ to be made up
of a thin cylindrical bar of radius ‘a’ and a
concentric thin cylindrical shell of radius ‘b’
filled in between with an electrolyte of
resistivity $ρ$ (see figure). If the battery is
connected to a resistance of value R, the
maximum Joule heating in R will take place for :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In this coaxial cylindrical battery, the current flows radially through the electrolyte between the inner cylindrical electrode of radius $a$ and the outer cylindrical shell of radius $b$, all along the length $l$.

Consider a thin coaxial cylindrical shell of electrolyte at a radial distance $r$ (where $a\leq r\leq b$), of radial thickness $dr$ and axial length $l$.


[IMG]


The curved surface area of this shell, perpendicular to the radial flow of current at radius $r$, is $A(r)=2πrl$.

The resistance of a uniform conductor of length $dL$ along the direction of the current and cross-sectional area $A$ is $dR_{\text{int}}=\dfrac{ρdL}{A}$.

Here the path length along the radial current is $dL=dr$ and the area perpendicular to the current is $A(r)=2πrl$, so the internal resistance of this thin shell is

$dr_{\text{int}}=\frac{ρdr}{2πrl}$

Since the radial current passes through every concentric cylindrical shell from $r=a$ to $r=b$, all these shells are in series, so the total internal resistance $r_{\text{int}}$ of the battery is the integral of $dr_{\text{int}}$ from $r=a$ to $r=b$.

$r_{\text{int}}=\int\limits _{a}^{b}\frac{ρdr}{2πrl}=\frac{ρ}{2πl}\int\limits _{a}^{b}\frac{1}{r}dr$

$r_{\text{int}}=\frac{ρ}{2πl}[\ln r]_{a}^{b}=\frac{ρ}{2πl}(\ln b-\ln a)=\frac{ρ}{2πl}\ln \left (\frac{b}{a}\right )$

Now let the battery, of emf $E$ and internal resistance $r_{\text{int}}$, be connected across the external resistor $R$. By Ohm's law, the current in the circuit is $I=\dfrac{E}{R+r_{\text{int}}}$.

By Joule's law of heating, the rate of heat generation (power $P$) in the external resistor $R$ is

$P=I^{2}R=\left (\frac{E}{R+r_{\text{int}}}\right )^{2}R=\frac{E^{2}R}{\left (R+r_{\text{int}}\right )^{2}}$

For the value of $R$ that maximises $P$, $\dfrac{dP}{dR}=0$.

$\frac{dP}{dR}=E^{2}\frac{d}{dR}\left [R\left (R+r_{\text{int}}\right )^{-2}\right ]=0$

$E^{2}\left [(1)\left (R+r_{\text{int}}\right )^{-2}+R(-2)\left (R+r_{\text{int}}\right )^{-3}(1)\right ]=0$

$E^{2}\left (R+r_{\text{int}}\right )^{-3}\left [\left (R+r_{\text{int}}\right )-2R\right ]=0$

$r_{\text{int}}-R=0\Rightarrow R=r_{\text{int}}$

The power $P$ is zero at $R=0$ and tends to zero as $R\to \infty$, so this single stationary point is the maximum.

$R=r_{\text{int}}=\frac{ρ}{2πl}\ln \left (\frac{b}{a}\right )$

Therefore, the Joule heating in $R$ is maximum when $R=\dfrac{ρ}{2πl}\ln \left (\dfrac{b}{a}\right )$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Moment of inertia of a cylinder of mass M,
length L and radius R about an axis passing
through its centre and perpendicular to the
axis of the cylinder is
 I = $M\left (\frac{R^{2}}{4}+\frac{L^{2}}{12}\right )$. If such a
cylinder is to be made for a given mass of a
material, the ratio $\frac{L}{R}$ for it to have minimum
possible I is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Given I = $M\left (\frac{R^{2}}{4}+\frac{L^{2}}{12}\right )$

M = $ρ$.V = $ρπR^{2}L$

$\Rightarrow$ $R^{2} =$ $\frac{M}{ρπL}$

$\therefore$ I = $M\left (\frac{M}{4ρπL}+\frac{L^{2}}{12}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dI}{dL}$ = $M\left (\frac{M}{4ρπ}\left (-\frac{1}{L^{2}}\right )-\frac{2L}{12}\right )$

For minimum I, $\frac{dI}{dL}=0$

$\therefore$ $M\left (\frac{M}{4ρπ}\left (-\frac{1}{L^{2}}\right )-\frac{2L}{12}\right )$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{M^{2}}{4ρπL^{2}}=\frac{2LM}{12}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{M}{4ρπL^{2}}=\frac{L}{6}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{ρπR^{2}L}{4ρπL^{2}}=\frac{L}{6}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{R^{2}}{L^{2}}=\frac{2}{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{R}{L}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{L}{R}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}$

A 750 Hz, 20 V (rms) source is connected to a
resistance of 100 $\Omega$, an inductance of 0.1803 H
and a capacitance of 10 $μ$F all in series. The
time in which the resistance (heat capacity
$2 J/^{o}C)$ will get heated by $10^{o}C. ($assume no loss
of heat to the surroudnings) is close to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f = 750 Hz, V_{$rms} = 20 V,

R = 100 $\Omega$, L = 0.1803 H,

C = 10$μ$ F, S = 2 J/°C

|Z| = $\sqrt{R^{2}+(X_{L}-X_{C})^{2}}$

= $\sqrt{R^{2}+\left (ωL-\frac{1}{ωC}\right )^{2}}$

= $\sqrt{R^{2}+\left (2πfL-\frac{1}{2πfC}\right )^{2}}$

= $\sqrt{(100)^{2}+\left (2\times 3.14\times 750\times 0.1803-\frac{1}{2\times 3.14\times 750\times 10^{-5}}\right )^{2}}$

 = 834 $\Omega$

In AC, power $(P) = i_{$rms$}V_{$rms} cos $𝜙$

 and $i_{$rms} = $\frac{V_{rms}}{|Z|}$

Power factor (cos $𝜙$) = $\frac{R}{|Z|}$

$\therefore$ P = $\frac{V_{rms}}{|Z|}.V_{rms}.\frac{R}{|Z|}$

= $\left (\frac{V_{rms}}{|Z|}\right )^{2}R$

= $\left (\frac{20}{834}\right )^{2}\times 100$

= 0.0575 J/S

Also, H = Pt = S$\Deltaθ$

$\Rightarrow$ t = $\frac{2(10)}{0.0575}$ = 348 sec

text:
A satellite is moving in a low nearly circular orbit around the earth. Its radius is roughly equal to
that of the earth’s radius $R_{e}$
. By firing rockets attached to it, its speed is instantaneously increased
in the direction of its motion so that it become $\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}$
 times larger. Due to this the farthest distance
from the centre of the earth that the satellite reaches is R. Value of R is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the low circular orbit, $v_{0}=\sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{R_{e}}}$; after firing, the speed is $v=\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}v_{0}$, perpendicular to the radius.


[IMG]

At the farthest point, at distance $R$ (marked $R_{\max }$), the velocity $v^{'}$ is again perpendicular to the radius, so conservation of angular momentum gives

$v^{'}=\dfrac{vR_{e}}{R}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}\dfrac{v_{0}R_{e}}{R}$

Conservation of energy per unit mass, with $v_{0}^{2}=\dfrac{GM}{R_{e}}$:

$-\dfrac{GM}{R_{e}}+\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \dfrac{3}{2}\cdot \dfrac{GM}{R_{e}}=-\dfrac{GM}{R}+\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \dfrac{3}{2}\cdot \dfrac{GM}{R_{e}}\cdot \dfrac{R_{e}^{2}}{R^{2}}$

Dividing by $GM$:

$-\dfrac{1}{4R_{e}}=-\dfrac{1}{R}+\dfrac{3R_{e}}{4R^{2}}$

Multiplying by $4R^{2}R_{e}$:

$R^{2}-4R_{e}R+3R_{e}^{2}=0\Rightarrow (R-R_{e})(R-3R_{e})=0$

The root $R=R_{e}$ is the firing point (the nearest point), so the farthest distance is $R=3R_{e}$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
An elliptical loop having resistance R, of semi major axis a, and semi minor axis b is placed in
magnetic field as shown in the figure. If the loop is rotated about the x-axis with angular frequency
$ω$, the average power loss in the loop due to Joule heating is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The area of an ellipse with semi-major axis $a$ and semi-minor axis $b$ is $A=πab$.

At time $t=0$ the elliptical loop lies in the $xy$-plane, so its area vector $⃗{A}$ (normal to the plane of the loop) points along the $z$-axis, parallel to the uniform magnetic field $⃗{B}=B\hat{k}$ (angle $θ=0$).


[IMG]


When the loop rotates about the $x$-axis with constant angular frequency $ω$, the angle $θ$ between the area vector $⃗{A}$ (normal to the loop) and the fixed magnetic field $⃗{B}$ increases linearly with time $t$,

$θ(t)=ωt$

The magnetic flux through the elliptical loop at any instant $t$ is the dot product of $⃗{B}$ and $⃗{A}$,

$\Phi (t)=⃗{B}\cdot ⃗{A}=BA\cos θ=B(πab)\cos (ωt)$

By Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the instantaneous emf $e(t)$ induced in the loop is the negative of the time rate of change of the magnetic flux,

$e(t)=-\frac{d\Phi }{dt}=-\frac{d}{dt}[πabB\cos (ωt)]$

Since $π$, $a$, $b$ and $B$ are constants, $e(t)=-πabB[-ω\sin (ωt)]=πabBω\sin (ωt)$.

By Ohm's law, the instantaneous induced current in the closed loop of resistance $R$ is $i(t)=\dfrac{e(t)}{R}=\dfrac{πabBω}{R}\sin (ωt)$.

By Joule's law of heating, the instantaneous power dissipated as heat in the loop at time $t$ is

$P(t)=[i(t)]^{2}R=\left (\frac{πabBω}{R}\sin (ωt)\right )^{2}R=\frac{π^{2}a^{2}b^{2}B^{2}ω^{2}}{R}\sin ^{2}(ωt)$

The average power loss over one complete rotation, of period $T=\dfrac{2π}{ω}$, is

$P_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{T}\int\limits _{0}^{T}P(t)dt=\frac{π^{2}a^{2}b^{2}B^{2}ω^{2}}{R}\left [\frac{1}{T}\int\limits _{0}^{T}\sin ^{2}(ωt)dt\right ]$

The average value of $\sin ^{2}(ωt)$ over one full period $T$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}$, so

$P_{\text{avg}}=\left (\frac{π^{2}a^{2}b^{2}B^{2}ω^{2}}{R}\right )\times \frac{1}{2}=\frac{π^{2}a^{2}b^{2}B^{2}ω^{2}}{2R}$

Therefore, the average power loss in the loop due to Joule heating is $\dfrac{π^{2}a^{2}b^{2}B^{2}ω^{2}}{2R}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
A uniform thin rope of length 12 m and mass 6 kg hangs vertically from a rigid support and a block
of mass 2 kg is attached to its free end. A transverse short wavetrain of wavelength 6 cm is
produced at the lower end of the rope. What is the wavelength of the wavetrain (in cm) when it
reaches the top of the rope ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$T_{1} = 2g$

$T_{2} = 8g$ 

V = $\sqrt{\frac{T}{μ}}$

$\therefore$ V $\propto$ $\sqrt{T}$

Also V = f$λ$

$\therefore$ $V_{1} = f_{1}λ_{1}$

and $V_{2} = f_{2}λ_{2}$

We know frequency of sources are same.

$\therefore$ $f_{1} = f_{2}$

So $\sqrt{\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}}=\frac{λ_{1}}{λ_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{\frac{2g}{8g}}=\frac{6}{λ_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ_{2}$ = 12 cm

text:
A block of mass m = 1 kg slides with velocity v = 6 m/s on a frictionless horizontal surface and
collides with a uniform vertical rod and sticks to it as shown. The rod is pivoted about O and swings
as a result of the collision making angle $θ$ before momentarily coming to rest. If the rod has mass
M = 2 kg, and length $l$ = 1 m, the value of $θ$ is approximately :

(take $g = 10 m/s^{2})$

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Applying Angular momentum conservation

mv$l$ = $\left (\frac{Ml^{2}}{3}+ml^{2}\right )ω$

$\Rightarrow$ $ω=\frac{1\times 6\times 1}{\frac{2}{3}+1}$ = $\frac{18}{5}$

Now, using energy conservation

$\frac{1}{2}Iω^{2}=(m+M)gh$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{Ml^{2}}{3}+ml^{2}\right )ω^{2}=(m+M)gx_{COM}(1-\cos θ)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{2}{3}+1\right )\left (\frac{18}{5}\right )^{2}=(m+M)g\times \frac{M\times \frac{l}{2}+ml}{(M+m)}(1-\cos θ)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{5}{3}\times \frac{18\times 18}{25}=10\times \left (2\times \frac{1}{2}+1\right )(1-\cos θ)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{5}{6}\times \frac{18\times 18}{25}=20(1-\cos θ)$

$\Rightarrow$ $(1-\cos θ)=\frac{18}{5}\times \frac{3}{20}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\cos θ=1-\frac{27}{50}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\cos θ=\frac{23}{50}$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ$ $\simeq$ $63^{o}$

 volume

temperature is varied. If $γ_{(beaker)}$ $= 6 × 10^{–6} ^{o}C^{–1}$ and $γ_{(mercury)}$ $= 1.5 × 10^{–4} ^{o}C^{–1}$, where $γ$ is the
coefficient of volume expansion, then $V_{m}$
 (in cc) is close to $____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Delta$V = V$γ\Delta$T

$\therefore$ $V_{1}γ_{1}$ $= V_{2}γ_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 500 $\times$ 6 $\times$ $10^{-6} = V_{m}$
 $\times$ 1.5 $\times$ $10^{-4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $V_{m} =$ $\frac{500\times 6\times 10^{-6}}{1.5\times 10^{-4}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $V_{m} = 20 cc$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
A cricket ball of mass 0.15 kg is thrown
vertically up by a bowling machine so that it
rises to a maximum height of 20 m after leaving
the machine. If the part pushing the ball applies
a constant force F on the ball and moves
horizontally a distance of 0.2 m while launching
the ball, the value of F (in N) is $(g = 10 ms^{–2})$
$____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Initial velocity, v = $\sqrt{2gh}$

= $\sqrt{2\times 10\times 20}$

= 20 m/s

Now work done by the machine,

$W_{F} =$ $\Delta$k

$\Rightarrow$ F.d = $\Delta$k

$\Rightarrow$ F = $\frac{\Delta k}{d}$

= $\frac{\frac{1}{2}\times 0.15\times 400-0}{0.2}$

= 150 N
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
When a long glass capillary tube of radius
0.015 cm is dipped in a liquid, the liquid rises
to a height of 15 cm within it. If the contact angle
between the liquid and glass to close to $0^{o}$, the
surface tension of the liquid, in milliNewton m–1,
is [$ρ_{(liquid)}$ = 900 kgm$^{–3}, g = 10 ms^{–2}$] 
(Give answer
in closest integer$) _____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Capillary rise

h = $\frac{2T\cos θ}{ρgr}$

$\Rightarrow$ T = $\frac{ρgrh}{2\cos θ}$

= $\frac{(900)(10)\left (15\times 10^{-5}\right )\left (15\times 10^{-2}\right )}{2}$

= 1012.5 $\times$ $10^{–4}$

$= 101.25 × 10^{–3}$
= 101.25 mN/m

$\simeq$ 101.00 mN/m
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
A person of 80 kg mass is standing on the rim
of a circular platform of mass 200 kg rotating
about its axis at 5 revolutions per minute (rpm).
The person now starts moving towards the
centre of the platform. What will be the
rotational speed (in rpm) of the platform when
the person reaches its centre $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I_{1}ω_{1}=I_{2}ω_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\frac{MR^{2}}{2}+mR^{2}\right )ω_{1}=\frac{MR^{2}}{2}ω_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (1+\frac{2mR^{2}}{MR^{2}}\right )ω_{1}=ω_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (1+\frac{2\times 80}{200}\right )ω_{1}=ω_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $ω_{2}=(1.8)ω_{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2$πf_{2} = 2πf_{1}$ $\times$ 1.8

$\Rightarrow$ $f_{2} = 5$ $\times$ 1.8 = 9
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
An observer can see through a small hole on the side of a jar (radius 15 cm) at a point at height of
15 cm from the bottom (see figure). The hole is at a height of 45 cm. When the jar is filled with a
liquid up to a height of 30 cm the same observer can see the edge at the bottom of the jar. If the
refractive index of the liquid is N/100, where N is an integer, the value of N is $_____$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


tan r = $\frac{15}{30}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$

sin r = $\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$

$1\sin  45^{o} =$ $μ$sin r

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=μ\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $μ$ = $\sqrt{\frac{5}{2}}$ = 1.58

$μ=\frac{N}{100}$ = 1.58

$\Rightarrow$ N = 158
